messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sam Welles <sam.welles@brightmart.com>, BrightMart Platform <platform@brightmart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Recap: Burst capacity & SLO priming — next steps

Hi Sam / BrightMart team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciated the clear requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared alignment: 

Key SLOs and targets (customer stated):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end (streaming) <= 200ms for short completions (<= 64 tokens).
- Streaming chunk latency: < 50ms between partial frames to the client.
- Throughput: sustained 600 req/s during peak windows; peak spikes to 1,200 req/s for short bursts.
- Concurrency: ability to handle 250 concurrent active streams without degraded p95.
- Acceptable queueing behavior: allow transient queue up to 60s for backpressure events; prefer graceful degradation (retries + 503 surge signals) vs silent failures.

Burst / autoscale expectations we captured:
- Warm pool: request for ~20 prewarmed instances in us-west-2 for production; target spin-up from cold to warm <= 30s.
- Scale-up plan: automated fast-path scaling for sudden +50% traffic within 60s; fallback routing to a slightly lower-cost variant if hit capacity limits.
- Priming behavior: retain KV cache for 120s after idle; suggested prefix priming of common prompts during warmup.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Redwood to run a targeted benchmark using your representative prompt set and traffic profile (synthetic mix: 70% short completions, 30% streaming long tails) — deliverables: latency/throughput curves, concurrency behavior, and a warm-pool sizing suggestion.
2) Schedule a 90-minute SRE workshop next week (deep dive into queueing behavior, priming hooks, and observability).
3) Redwood SE (Marissa) to prepare a short playbook and priming script we can run in a Dedicated trial environment; Pricing/Product (Lauren) to provide a ballpark for a 2-week canary (Dedicated reservation + burst buffer).
4) Share drive folder with test plan and initial playbook.

Attachments we will push to the shared folder: priming-playbook-v1.pdf (walkthrough), warm-pool-latency-test-results.csv (example output), and an initial quote (bm-deal-quote-4832.pdf).

If that all looks good, Sam — can you confirm the most representative 10 prompts we should start with and whether the 20-instance warm pool is acceptable as a starting point? Also tell us your preferred day/time for the SRE workshop (we have slots Tues/Wed next week).

Thanks,

--

Jordan / team — I put together the initial priming playbook and a short test plan. Attached: priming-playbook-v1.pdf (walkthrough) and warm-pool-latency-test-results.csv (example output from a 20-instance warm pool synthetic run). Notes/highlights: 

- Priming approach: warm instances by sequential prefix priming and a short KV touch pass. KV retention configured to 120s for the trial; we observed that retention > 90s materially reduces p95 on resumed streams.
- Warm pool sizing: 10/20/40 baseline runs show diminishing returns after ~25 prewarmed instances for the model family they plan to use. Will deliver the full curves.
- Spin-up measurement: cold->instance-ready averaged 18s, but cold->streaming-ready (KV primed, prefix primed) averaged 46s in our synthetic flow. We can tune priming to reach ~28–32s with more aggressive parallel priming at cost of temporary CPU consumption during warmup.
- Queueing behavior: recommend queue time SLAs and a graceful 503 with Retry-After for spikes exceeding 120% of provisioned capacity.

Planned next steps:
1) Run the BrightMart prompt set (when Sam sends it) against 10/20/40 runs — schedule Wed 2027-05-18 morning.
2) Produce a short MOP and a staging script for the Dedicated canary.
3) Share detailed results prior to the Wed workshop.

Attaching the playbook and sample CSV to this thread (stubs referenced in attachments metadata).

Thanks,
